summary.text: Rick Edmonds is a Baptist pastor and Republican state senator from Baton Rouge who served in the Louisiana House from 2016 to 2024 and now chairs the Senate Education Committee.
He originally announced for the 5th Congressional District and qualified for the 6th District in August 2026 after the maps were redrawn.

paragraphs.text: Edmonds was born on September 12, 1956, in Shreveport, Louisiana, and lives in Baton Rouge.
He earned a B.A. from East Texas Baptist University in 1979 and a Master of Divinity from New Orleans Baptist Theological Seminary in 1990.

A pastor, he has served churches including Calvary Baptist Church in Shreveport and is currently senior pastor of First Baptist Church of McComb, Mississippi, a position he says he commutes to while living in the 6th District.
According to Wikipedia, he was also previously involved with the Louisiana Family Forum.
Edmonds won Louisiana House District 66 in 2015, defeating Republican incumbent Darrell Ourso, and served from January 2016 to January 2024.
In the 2018 special election for Louisiana Secretary of State, he finished fourth with 11% of the vote.
Edmonds won Louisiana Senate District 6 in 2023, defeating Rep. Barry Ivey with 62% of the vote, and took office on January 8, 2024.
He chairs the Senate Education Committee in 2025-2026 and also serves on the Insurance, Judiciary A and Finance committees.
After announcing for the 5th Congressional District, he qualified for the 6th District in August 2026 once the May elections were canceled and the maps redrawn.
